name: Train Subdivision/District List
description: This message is sent to the Locomotive to provide a list of PTC subdivisions/districts for which the Locomotive needs mandatory directives. It is sent in response to the Request Train Subdivision/District List (02007) message. It also is sent unsolicited if the Office receives a change in the train subdivision/district list to distribute to the Locomotive. The Locomotive confirms receipt of an unsolicited message with the Confirmation of Train Subdivision/District List (02008) message.

CRC-32 around the Track Data

name: Office Segment Poll
description: This message is sent by the Office to the Locomotive to provide information on the current set of mandatory directives and track data for one or more subdivisions/districts and the status of control points for which the Locomotive has registered within those subdivisions/districts. The Locomotive registers for polls for a specific subdivision/district with the Poll Registration (02020) message.

fields.description: Railroad SCAC of the railroad to which the poll registration was sent, left-justified space filled
CRC calculated over the train subdivision/district list received in the Train Subdivision/District List message
CRC calculated over the list of configuration versions in the Configuration Version List (01005) message
Number of PTC subdivisions or districts up to 60
PTC subdivision/district identifier (1 to 65535)
CRC calculated over track data and all mandatory directive datasets and text for the subdivision/district that are expected to be onboard
An ever-changing value that is included in the Composite CRC
CRC calculated over RIC Authority CRCs and RIC Bulletin CRCs

design_notes.A: When the ‘Office state’ field is set to ‘3 = Synchronizing,’ the ‘Dataset CRC’ is set to zero for that subdivision/district.
design_notes.B: When the ‘Office state’ field is set to ‘4 = No CAD support,’ the ‘Dataset CRC’ is calculated over a null list of movement authorities and bulletins for that subdivision/district.
design_notes.C: If the message contains only subdivisions/districts with the ‘Office state’ field set to ‘4 = No CAD support,’ the ‘Train Subdivision/District List CRC’ is set to zero.
design_notes.D: The ‘Configuration Version List CRC’ field is populated with the Configuration Version List CRC calculated in the Configuration Version List (01005) message.
design_notes.E: The table below shows the fields over which the ‘Dataset CRC’ is calculated in order. Field Size (bytes) Type Description Repeated for each movement authority stored by the Office for the locomotive to which it is sending the Office Segment Poll (01021) message Note i PTC Authority Reference Number 4 Numeric Note ii CRC around Authority Dataset 4 CRC-32 Repeated for each bulletin stored by the Office for the Locomotive to which it is sending the Office Segment Poll (01021) message Note iv PTC Bulletin Reference Number 4 Numeric Note iii CRC Around Bulletin Dataset 4 CRC-32 For the track data for the subdivision/district Track Data Version 4 Numeric CRC around Track Data 4 CRC-32 i. The onboard segment calculates a Dataset CRC over the datasets it has stored in the same order. ii. The authority datasets are ordered from least to greatest ‘PTC Authority Reference Number.’ When there is more than one movement authority with the same PTC Authority Reference Number, the original authority is first, followed by the modified authority. iii. The bulletin datasets are ordered from least to greatest ‘PTC Bulletin Reference Number.’ iv. Canceled bulletins awaiting crew acknowledgment are not included.
design_notes.F: The on-board segment will use the CRCs as defined in WEG-ICD-11289 RIC CRC Definitions Addendum for I-ETMS Protect when RIC is present.
design_notes.G: If RIC functionality is not present in the Office, RIC Uniqueness Index and Composite CRC are populated with zeros.

name: Train Consist
description: This message is sent to the Locomotive to provide Consist data. This message is sent in response to the Request Train Consist (02030) message. It also is sent unsolicited when the Office has new Consist data to distribute to the Locomotive. The Locomotive confirms receipt of the message with a Confirmation of Train Consist (02031) message.

enumeration.1: Response to locomotive request with CAD provided consist
enumeration.2: Response to locomotive request, no consist data available

fields.description: Railroad SCAC of the railroad to which the request for train consist was sent, left-justified space filled
All locomotive identifiers in train (1 to 24)
Locomotive ID
Position of the locomotive in the train (1 to 999)
Short tons (50 to 400)
Feet (40 to 150)
Horsepower (0 to 10,000)
Short tons (0 to 45,000)
Operative brakes (0 to 999)
Axles excluding the locomotives listed under the ‘Number of Locomotives’ field above (0 to 3996)
Total train length (locomotives and cars) (40 to 25,000 ft)
Total braking force for the train excluding the locomotives listed under the ‘Number of Locomotives’ field above (0 to 30,000,000 lbs)
0 to 125 mph
All train restriction types associated with the train (0 – 32)
0: Unknown 1 – 32: Numeric type which corresponds to the numeric type assigned to the train restrictions defined in the track data

design_notes.A: If the ‘Reason for Sending’ is ‘2 = Response to locomotive request, no consist data available,’ the rest of the fields are populated as described below: Train Type 0 Lead Locomotive Orientation 0 Number of Locomotives 0 Trailing Tonnage through Maximum Train Speed 0
design_notes.B: To indicate that a numeric parameter is unknown, the value of that parameter is set to any number that fits in the field size allowed for that parameter but is outside of the allowable range specified in the description of that parameter. For example, a ‘Number of Locomotives’ of 0 or any number between 25 and 255 indicates that the number of locomotives is unknown. Similarly, a ‘Loaded Car Count’ between 1000 and 65535 indicates that the loaded car count is unknown.
design_notes.C: If there is no equipment speed restriction associated with the train, the ‘Maximum Train Speed’ is populated with zero.
design_notes.D: If train restriction type is not available from the railroad office system providing the summary consist data, the ‘Number of Train Restriction Types’ field is set to one (1) and the ‘Train Restriction Type’ field is set to zero (0).

design_notes.A: The ‘Displayable Bulletin Reference Number’ field contains the original bulletin reference number assigned to the bulletin by CAD or another back office system, which may be displayed in prompts to the crew by the onboard segment.
design_notes.B: The ‘Number of Speed Restrictions’ field is populated with zero for track-out-of-service bulletins, advisory/cautionary bulletins, work zones with no associated speed reduction, and PTC suspension bulletins.
design_notes.C: For PTC grade-crossing bulletins, a 0 mph speed restriction indicates an activation failure, and a non-zero speed restriction indicates a false activation.
design_notes.D: For bulletins other than type Critical Alert, the ‘Time to Comply’ field is populated with 0.
design_notes.E: For bulletins that do not include a start time, the ‘Effective Time Stamp’ field is populated with a zero.
design_notes.F: For bulletins that do not include an end time, the ‘Expire Time Stamp’ field is populated with a zero.
design_notes.G: For bulletins that are always in effect between the start time and the end time, the ‘Number of Time of Day Filters’ is populated with a zero.
design_notes.H: For a bulletin that is not continuously in effect but is in effect within a time range on every day of the week, the ‘Number of Time of Day Filters’ is set to 7, and a separate Time of Day Filter is included for each day.
design_notes.I: Bulletins with a non-zero ‘Number of Speed Restrictions’ may either contain one speed restriction applicable to all trains or speed restrictions applicable to specific train types but not both.
design_notes.J: When the ‘Time of Day End Time Stamp’ is set to an earlier time than the ‘Time of Day Start Time Stamp’ for a Time of Day Filter, the ‘Time of Day End Time Stamp’ is applied to the day following the ‘Time of Day Filter Day of Week’ specified for that Time of Day Filter. This allows a restriction that spans midnight to be specified with a single Time of Day filter.
design_notes.K: For bulletins at a single point, the ‘Segment Starting Milepost’ and ‘Segment Ending Milepost’ fields are populated with the same location.
design_notes.L: For bulletins where the ‘Restricted Speed’ field is set to 1 (Yes), the onboard segment will enforce the lower of the non-zero value in the ‘Speed’ field or the configurable value stored onboard. If the ‘Speed’ field is populated with zero, the onboard segment will enforce the configurable value stored onboard.
design_notes.M: For bulletins other than of type ‘Speed Restriction,’ the 'Direction field is populated with ‘1 = Enforceable in both directions.’
design_notes.N: For bulletins for which a direction is not an attribute in the message from Dispatch, the ‘Direction’ field is populated with ‘1 = Enforceable in both directions.’
design_notes.O: A bulletin may be defined with a track designation of “ALL” if the starting milepost is the same as the ending milepost and that milepost exists on every track over which the bulletin is to be applied. Otherwise, each track name must be listed in a separate bulletin segment.
design_notes.P: When the bulletin track designation is “ALL,” the “ALL” Track Flag field is set to true, the ‘Segment Track Name Length’ is set to zero. When the bulletin track designation is not “ALL,” the “ALL” Track Flag field is set to false.
design_notes.Q: For bulletins that do not specify a crossing by DOT ID, the ‘DOT ID’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20).
design_notes.R: For bulletins that specify a crossing by DOT ID, the ‘Number of Bulletin Segments’ is set to zero. Only bulletins of type ‘Grade crossing’ may be specified with a DOT ID.
design_notes.S: The ‘Body of Summary Text’ field contains one line of text to be displayed as part of a list on the onboard display.
design_notes.T: The on-board segment will use the CRCs as defined in WEG-ICD-11289 RIC CRC Definitions Addendum for I-ETMS Protect when RIC is present. If RIC functionality is not present in the Office, RIC Bulletin CRC is populated with zeros.
design_notes.U: For bulletins of type “Advisory/Cautionary”, the “Number of Bulletin Segments” is set to zero.

design_notes.A: The ‘Displayable Movement Authority Reference Number’ field contains the original movement authority reference number assigned to the movement authority by CAD or another back office system, which may be displayed in prompts to the crew by the onboard segment.
design_notes.B: See the specific railroad Back Office Segment Specification for details on how fields in this message are populated based on the type(s) of authorities employed by the railroad.
design_notes.C: For authorities where the ‘Authority Segment Direction’ is ‘Unidirectional,’ the ‘Starting Milepost’ in the ‘For each authority segment’ loop represents the milepost closest to the ‘From limit’ of the authority, and the ‘Ending Milepost’ represents the milepost closest to the ‘To limit.’
design_notes.D: For authority to enter main track and authority to pass signal at stop, the authority limits represent the route the train is authorized to travel upon entering main track or passing the signal at stop.
design_notes.E: In order for the onboard segment to report when an authority of type ‘Enter main track’ or ‘Pass signal at stop’ has been used with an EMT/PSS Authority Used Notification (02054) message, the 01051 message must contain at least one authority segment that contains the point at which the train will enter the main track or pass the signal at stop.
design_notes.F: When the ‘Number of Authority Segments’ field is set to zero, the ‘Track Limit CRC’ field is also set to zero.
design_notes.G: Order for calculating Track Limit CRC: Field Size (bytes) Type Description Repeat per ‘Number of Authority Segments’ Repeat per Number of Blocks identified in the Authority Segment Note i Railroad SCAC 4 Printable ASCII Subdivision/District ID 2 Numeric Block ID 4 Numeric Starting Offset 4 Numeric Note ii Ending Offset 4 Numeric i. To build a Block List, begin at the ‘Starting Milepost’ and traverse to the ‘Ending Milepost.’ When a starting or ending milepost of an authority segment is located at the starting or ending offset of a block, then that limit may also be identified in the starting or ending offset of the adjacent block. If the milepost measure values of the adjacent blocks are identical, only one of the adjacent blocks should be included in the CRC calculation. Conditions for whether adjacent blocks at the start or end of an authority segment should be included in the CRC calculation are listed below. design_notes.J: For movement authorities where the ‘Authority Restriction Type’ is set to ‘1 = Joint with train,’ ‘2 = Joint with men and equipment,’ and ‘3 = Joint (Unspecified),’ the ‘Speed’ field is set to zero. The onboard segment applies a restricted speed limit per the onboard segment requirements.

design_notes.N: If no joint authority holder identification is available, the ‘Joint Authority Holder Length’ field is set to zero.

DESIGN NOTES:
A. The ‘Displayable Movement Authority Reference Number’ field contains the original movement authority
reference number assigned to the movement authority by CAD or another back office system, which may be
displayed in prompts to the crew by the onboard segment.
B. See the specific railroad Back Office Segment Specification for details on how fields in this message are
populated based on the type(s) of authorities employed by the railroad.
C. For authorities where the ‘Authority Segment Direction’ is ‘Unidirectional,’ the ‘Starting Milepost’ in the ‘For
each authority segment’ loop represents the milepost closest to the ‘From limit’ of the authority, and the
‘Ending Milepost’ represents the milepost closest to the ‘To limit.’
D. For authority to enter main track and authority to pass signal at stop, the authority limits represent the
route the train is authorized to travel upon entering main track or passing the signal at stop.
E. In order for the onboard segment to report when an authority of type ‘Enter main track’ or ‘Pass signal at
stop’ has been used with an EMT/PSS Authority Used Notification (02054) message, the 01051 message
must contain at least one authority segment that contains the point at which the train will enter the main track
or pass the signal at stop.
F. When the ‘Number of Authority Segments’ field is set to zero, the ‘Track Limit CRC’ field is also set to zero.
G. Order for calculating Track Limit CRC:

or ending milepost of an authority segment is located at the starting or ending offset of a block, then that limit
may also be identified in the starting or ending offset of the adjacent block. If the milepost measure values of
the adjacent blocks are identical, only one of the adjacent blocks should be included in the CRC calculation.

The following conventions apply:
• Milepost limits of an authority segment are represented by AuthMP (start) to AuthMP (end).
• Milepost values at the start and end of a block are represented by BlkMP (A, start) and BlkMP (A, end).
• Blocks A and B are adjacent, where BlkMP (A, end) is the same physical location as BlkMP (B, start).
• Blocks are considered to be adjacent when the end points
o reference each other in previous and next element IDs, or
o reference the same switch in previous and next element IDs.
• When the authority segment has the same start and end milepost at a block boundary, onboard picks
the 0 offset block to associate with the milepost and compute the track limit CRC. If the authority
segment lies at 0 offset of both blocks, the lower-numbered index block is selected.
ii. The Offset order follows the MP direction derived from the ‘Starting Milepost’ and ‘Ending Milepost’ fields.
H. The ‘Signal PTC Subdivision/District ID,’ ‘Length of Site Name,’ ‘Length of Site Device ID,’ and ‘Device
Type’ fields are populated with zeros if the authority is not of type ‘Pass signal at stop,’ otherwise, they
identify the signal the train has authority to pass.
I. If any other authority type ends at a signal (e.g., track and time or track permit), the Office resolves that
location to a milepost.
J. For movement authorities where the ‘Authority Restriction Type’ is set to ‘1 = Joint with train,’ ‘2 = Joint with
men and equipment,’ and ‘3 = Joint (Unspecified),’ the ‘Speed’ field is set to zero. The onboard segment
applies a restricted speed limit per the onboard segment requirements.
K. The ‘Body of Summary Text’ field contains one line of text to be displayed as part of a list on the onboard
display.
L. The on-board segment will use the CRCs as defined in WEG-ICD-11289 RIC CRC Definitions Addendum
for I-ETMS Protect when RIC is present. If RIC functionality is not present in the Office, RIC Authority CRC is
populated with zeros.
M. The on-board segment will accept joint authority holder if populated, but full functionality (separate target
limits for movement authorities with different joint authority holders and applicable prompting) will not be
available until CAF 128447 is prioritized.
N. If no joint authority holder identification is available, the ‘Joint Authority Holder Length’ field is set to zero.
O. If an Authority OK Time was not provided by the railroad’s CAD, the ‘Authority OK Time Stamp’ is
populated with date ‘1/1/1970’ and time ‘00:00:00’.
P. If no “At” location is conveyed in the message, the “At Milepost”, “At Milepost Prefix Length”, “At Milepost
Suffix Length”, “At Track name Length”, and “PTC Subdivision/District ID” fields are populated with zero.

DESIGN NOTES:
A. The ‘Displayable Movement Authority Reference Number’ field contains the original movement authority
reference number assigned to the movement authority by CAD or another back office system, which may be
displayed in prompts to the crew by the onboard segment.
B. See the specific railroad Back Office Segment Specification for details on how fields in this message are
populated based on the type(s) of authorities employed by the railroad.
C. For authorities where the ‘Authority Segment Direction’ is ‘Unidirectional,’ the ‘Starting Milepost’ in the ‘For
each authority segment’ loop represents the milepost closest to the ‘From limit’ of the authority, and the
‘Ending Milepost’ represents the milepost closest to the ‘To limit.’
D. For authority to enter main track and authority to pass signal at stop, the authority limits represent the
route the train is authorized to travel upon entering main track or passing the signal at stop.
E. In order for the onboard segment to report when an authority of type ‘Enter main track’ or ‘Pass signal at
stop’ has been used with an EMT/PSS Authority Used Notification (02054) message, the 01051 message
must contain at least one authority segment that contains the point at which the train will enter the main track
or pass the signal at stop.
F. When the ‘Number of Authority Segments’ field is set to zero, the ‘Track Limit CRC’ field is also set to zero.
G. Order for calculating Track Limit CRC:

i. To build a Block List, begin at the ‘Starting Milepost’ and traverse to the ‘Ending Milepost.’ When a starting
or ending milepost of an authority segment is located at the starting or ending offset of a block, then that limit
may also be identified in the starting or ending offset of the adjacent block. If the milepost measure values of
the adjacent blocks are identical, only one of the adjacent blocks should be included in the CRC calculation.
Conditions for whether adjacent blocks at the start or end of an authority segment should be included in the

The following conventions apply:
• Milepost limits of an authority segment are represented by AuthMP (start) to AuthMP (end).
• Milepost values at the start and end of a block are represented by BlkMP (A, start) and BlkMP (A, end).
• Blocks A and B are adjacent, where BlkMP (A, end) is the same physical location as BlkMP (B, start).
• Blocks are considered to be adjacent when the end points
o reference each other in previous and next element IDs, or
o reference the same switch in previous and next element IDs.
• When the authority segment has the same start and end milepost at a block boundary, onboard picks
the 0 offset block to associate with the milepost and compute the track limit CRC. If the authority
segment lies at 0 offset of both blocks, the lower-numbered index block is selected.
ii. The Offset order follows the MP direction derived from the ‘Starting Milepost’ and ‘Ending Milepost’ fields.
H. The ‘Signal PTC Subdivision/District ID,’ ‘Length of Site Name,’ ‘Length of Site Device ID,’ and ‘Device
Type’ fields are populated with zeros if the authority is not of type ‘Pass signal at stop,’ otherwise, they
identify the signal the train has authority to pass.
I. If any other authority type ends at a signal (e.g., track and time or track permit), the Office resolves that
location to a milepost.
J. For movement authorities where the ‘Authority Restriction Type’ is set to ‘1 = Joint with train,’ ‘2 = Joint with
men and equipment,’ and ‘3 = Joint (Unspecified),’ the ‘Speed’ field is set to zero. The onboard segment
applies a restricted speed limit per the onboard segment requirements.
K. The ‘Body of Summary Text’ field contains one line of text to be displayed as part of a list on the onboard
display.
L. The on-board segment will use the CRCs as defined in WEG-ICD-11289 RIC CRC Definitions Addendum
for I-ETMS Protect when RIC is present. If RIC functionality is not present in the Office, RIC Authority CRC is
populated with zeros.
M. The on-board segment will accept joint authority holder if populated, but full functionality (separate target
limits for movement authorities with different joint authority holders and applicable prompting) will not be
available until CAF 128447 is prioritized.
N. If no joint authority holder identification is available, the ‘Joint Authority Holder Length’ field is set to zero.
O. If an Authority OK Time was not provided by the railroad’s CAD, the ‘Authority OK Time Stamp’ is
populated with date ‘1/1/1970’ and time ‘00:00:00’.
P. If no “At” location is conveyed in the message, the “At Milepost”, “At Milepost Prefix Length”, “At Milepost
Suffix Length”, “At Track name Length”, and “PTC Subdivision/District ID” fields are populated with zero.

name: File Part Checksum
description: This message is sent by the Office to provide information on the checksum over a portion of a file that is available for transfer to aid the locomotive in resuming download of the file. It is sent in response to the File Part Checksum Request (02102) message.

fields.description: Railroad SCAC of the railroad to which the file part checksum request was sent, left-justified space filled
Transaction identifier from the File Part Checksum Request message
Number of checksums (0 to 8) Repeated for each Checksum: Byte Count 4 Numeric Number of bytes that the MD5 sum covers starting at byte 0 of the file
MD5 sum over the first ‘Byte Count’ bytes of data

design_notes.A: The Office may use a delta value different from the Suggested Delta in the File Part Checksum Request message as long as all ‘Byte Count’ values are less than or equal to the Offset value. Byte Count values are decremented by the Suggested Delta, aligned on delta boundaries, where Offset > (Suggested Delta * N) ≥ (Offset – Suggested Delta): • Checksum(1).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 6) • Checksum(2).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 5) • Checksum(3).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 4) • Checksum(4).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 3) • Checksum(5).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 2) • Checksum(6).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 1) • Checksum(7).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N) • Checksum(8).Byte Count = Offset For example, if the Offset value in the 02102 message is 100,000 and the Suggested Delta is 4096, then the Byte Count values below would be used for generating the MD5 check- sums (N = 24, since 100,000 > (4096 * 24) ≥ 95,904): • Checksum(1).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 6) = 73,728 (0×12000) • Checksum(2).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 5) = 77, 824 (0×13000) • Checksum(3).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 4) = 81,920 (0×14000) • Checksum(4).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 3) = 86, 016 (0×15000) • Checksum(5).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 2) = 90,112 (0×16000) • Checksum(6).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 1) = 94,208 (0×17000) • Checksum(7).Byte Count = 4096 * (24) = 98,304 (0×18000) • Checksum(8).Byte Count = Offset = 100,000 (0×186a0)
design_notes.B: Only checksums for positive, non-zero ‘Byte Count’ values are included. If N > 6, Checksum Count is 8. If N ≤ 6, Checksum Count is N + 1. The Checksum list is ordered from smallest to largest byte count.

DESIGN NOTES:
A. The Office may use a delta value different from the Suggested Delta in the File Part Checksum Request
message as long as all ‘Byte Count’ values are less than or equal to the Offset value.
Byte Count values are decremented by the Suggested Delta, aligned on delta boundaries, where Offset >
(Suggested Delta * N) ≥ (Offset – Suggested Delta):
• Checksum(1).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 6)
• Checksum(2).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 5)
• Checksum(3).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 4)
• Checksum(4).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 3)
• Checksum(5).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 2)
• Checksum(6).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N – 1)
• Checksum(7).Byte Count = Suggested Delta * (N)
• Checksum(8).Byte Count = Offset
For example, if the Offset value in the 02102 message is 100,000 and the Suggested Delta is 4096, then the
Byte Count values below would be used for generating the MD5 check- sums (N = 24, since 100,000 > (4096
* 24) ≥ 95,904):
• Checksum(1).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 6) = 73,728 (0×12000)
• Checksum(2).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 5) = 77, 824 (0×13000)
• Checksum(3).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 4) = 81,920 (0×14000)
• Checksum(4).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 3) = 86, 016 (0×15000)
• Checksum(5).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 2) = 90,112 (0×16000)
• Checksum(6).Byte Count = 4096 * (24 – 1) = 94,208 (0×17000)
• Checksum(7).Byte Count = 4096 * (24) = 98,304 (0×18000)
• Checksum(8).Byte Count = Offset = 100,000 (0×186a0)
B. Only checksums for positive, non-zero ‘Byte Count’ values are included. If N > 6, Checksum Count is 8. If
N ≤ 6, Checksum Count is N + 1. The Checksum list is ordered from smallest to largest byte count.

design_notes.A: When the ‘Reason for Sending’ is ‘3 = Entered main track on authority manually indicated’ or ‘4 = Passed signal at stop on authority manually indicated,’ the ‘PTC Authority Reference Number’ and ‘CRC around Authority Dataset’ fields are set to zero.
design_notes.B: When the ‘Reason for Sending’ is ‘1 = Entered main track on authority received electronically’ or ‘3 = Entered main track on authority manually indicated,’ the ‘Site Name,’ ‘Site Device ID,’ and ‘Device Type’ fields identify the switch belonging to the clearance point at which the train entered main track. In the case where multiple switches share that same clearance point as identified in the track data, the onboard segment reports the first switch in advance of the train’s leading edge on the train’s calculated route. If the on-board segment cannot determine the device identity, the ‘Site Name Length’ and ‘Site Device ID Length’ fields are populated with zero.
design_notes.C: When the ‘Reason for Sending’ is ‘2 = Passed signal at stop on authority received electronically’ or ‘4 = Passed signal at stop on authority manually indicated,’ the ‘Site Name,’ ‘Site Device ID,’ and ‘Device Type’ fields identify the signal that the train passed.

design_notes.A: If the train’s leading edge does not currently occupy a form-based authority, the ‘Current PTC Authority Reference Number’ field is populated with zero.
design_notes.B: If the on-board segment does not have a track location, the ‘Head End Railroad SCAC’ and ‘Rear End Railroad SCAC’ fields are populated with ASCII spaces (0x20); the ‘Head End Milepost’, ‘Head End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Head End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Head End Milepost Track Name Length’, ‘Head End PTC Subdivision / District ID’, ‘Rear End Milepost’, ‘Rear End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Rear End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Rear End Track Name Length’, and ‘Rear End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ fields are populated with zero. If the onboard segment has a track location but does not have a known direction of movement, the ‘Rear End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with spaces and the ‘Rear End Milepost’, ‘Rear End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Rear End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Rear End Track Name Length’, and ‘Rear End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ fields are populated with zero.
design_notes.C: See Section 13 Data Dictionary for mapping between the ‘Locomotive State Summary’ and ‘Locomotive State’ fields.
design_notes.D: For details on which ‘Reason for Report’ enumerations are applicable to a specific railroad, see “Onboard Segment Requirement Specification,” which is provided by each Onboard PTC Application vendor. When the locomotive transitions between track blocks (5) or across a switch (7) and the transition is at a subdivision/district boundary, the ‘Reason for Report’ should be (8).
design_notes.E: When the Reason for Report is ‘0 = Requested by Office,’ the Time Elapsed Parameter and the Distance Elapsed Parameter are set to those values received in the 01080 message. Otherwise, they are set to zero.
design_notes.F: When the status of the Control Brake is not known, “Control Brake” is set to zero.
design_notes.G: When any part of the train is within the limits of an exclusion zone, the rear end track location will be reported as unknown as defined in Design note B.

10.37.1 Description
This message is sent from the Locomotive to the Office to provide a notification that the Locomotive has warned
or enforced the train for the specified reason. This message is sent to the employing, owning, and currently
located operating railroads.

DESIGN NOTES:
A. The ‘Warning Distance’ and ‘Braking Distance’ fields may be populated for an Enforcement type of
‘Reactive Enforcement’ but will not be meaningful in this case because the Locomotive is inside the target.
B. When the on-board segment has a Train ID stored for the railroad to which the message is being sent, the
‘Train ID’ field is set to that train ID. When the on-board segment does not have a Train ID stored for the
railroad to which the message is being sent, the ‘Train ID length’ is set to zero.
The On-board segment will not populate the Train ID information in the (02083) message when in the Failed
state and any active fault which causes the brakes to be applied gets cleared.
C. When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Enforcement due to system fault’, or ‘Parking mode
enforcement’ in the Target Information:
• the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’
• the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name
Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Target Speed’ is set to zero.
D. When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Restricted state overspeed warning’, or ‘Restricted state
overspeed enforcement’ in the Target Information:
• the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’
• the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name
Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20).
E. If no warning occurred in the Warning Information:
• the ‘Warning Time’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’
• the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero
• the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
F. If the system did not have a track location when warning started in the Warning Information:
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
G. If the system did not have a track location when enforcement braking started in the Enforcement
Information:
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
H. If no emergency enforcement braking occurred in the Emergency Enforcement Braking Information:
• the ‘Emergency Enforcement Braking Time’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’
• the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero
• the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
I. If the system does not have a track location when enforcement ends in the Current Information:
• the ‘Milepost’, ‘Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision
/ District ID’, and ‘Current Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
J. The ‘Target Code’ enumeration determines how the ‘Target Description’ field is populated, according to the
following list, where %keyword% indicates variable information available to the onboard segment and will be
replaced with the data in the same format as the corresponding field in the 02083 message expressed in

design_notes.A: The ‘Warning Distance’ and ‘Braking Distance’ fields may be populated for an Enforcement type of ‘Reactive Enforcement’ but will not be meaningful in this case because the Locomotive is inside the target.
design_notes.B: When the on-board segment has a Train ID stored for the railroad to which the message is being sent, the ‘Train ID’ field is set to that train ID. When the on-board segment does not have a Train ID stored for the railroad to which the message is being sent, the ‘Train ID length’ is set to zero. The On-board segment will not populate the Train ID information in the (02083) message when in the Failed state and any active fault which causes the brakes to be applied gets cleared.
design_notes.C: When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Enforcement due to system fault’, or ‘Parking mode enforcement’ in the Target Information: • the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’ • the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero • the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero • the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Target Speed’ is set to zero.
design_notes.D: When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Restricted state overspeed warning’, or ‘Restricted state overspeed enforcement’ in the Target Information: • the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’ • the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero • the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero • the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20).
design_notes.E: If no warning occurred in the Warning Information: • the ‘Warning Time’ is set to zero • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero • the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero • the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero • the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’ • the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero • the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
design_notes.F: If the system did not have a track location when warning started in the Warning Information: • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero • the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero • the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero • the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
design_notes.G: If the system did not have a track location when enforcement braking started in the Enforcement Information: • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero • the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero • the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero • the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
design_notes.H: If no emergency enforcement braking occurred in the Emergency Enforcement Braking Information: • the ‘Emergency Enforcement Braking Time’ is set to zero • the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero • the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero • the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero • the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’ • the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero • the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
design_notes.I: If the system does not have a track location when enforcement ends in the Current Information: • the ‘Milepost’, ‘Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Current Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero • the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20) • the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.

10.38.1 Description
This message is sent from the Locomotive to the Office to provide a notification that the Locomotive has warned
or enforced the train for the specified reason. This message is sent to the employing, owning, and currently
located operating railroads.
Version 135 of this message is to indicate certain fields are metric.

DESIGN NOTES:
A. The ‘Warning Distance’ and ‘Braking Distance’ fields may be populated for an Enforcement type of
‘Reactive Enforcement’ but will not be meaningful in this case because the Locomotive is inside the target.
B. When the on-board segment has a Train ID stored for the railroad to which the message is being sent, the
‘Train ID’ field is set to that train ID. When the on-board segment does not have a Train ID stored for the
railroad to which the message is being sent, the ‘Train ID length’ is set to zero.
The On-board segment will not populate the Train ID information in the (02083) message when in the Failed
state and any active fault which causes the brakes to be applied gets cleared.
C. When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Enforcement due to system fault’, or ‘Parking mode
enforcement’ in the Target Information:
• the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’
• the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name
Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Target Speed’ is set to zero.
D. When the ‘Warning/Enforcement Type’ is ‘Restricted state overspeed warning’, or ‘Restricted state
overspeed enforcement’ in the Target Information:
• the ‘Target Category’ is set to ‘0 – No target’
• the ‘Length of Target Description’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, and ‘Start PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘Start Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘End Milepost’, ‘End Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘End Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘End Track Name
Length’, and ‘End PTC Subdivision / District ID’ are set to zero
• the ‘End Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20).
E. If no warning occurred in the Warning Information:
• the ‘Warning Time’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’
• the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero
• the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
F. If the system did not have a track location when warning started in the Warning Information:
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Warning Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
G. If the system did not have a track location when enforcement braking started in the Enforcement
Information:
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
H. If no emergency enforcement braking occurred in the Emergency Enforcement Braking Information:
• the ‘Emergency Enforcement Braking Time’ is set to zero
• the ‘Start Milepost’, ‘Start Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Start Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Start Track Name
Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision / District ID’, and ‘Start Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Braking Distance’ is set to zero
• the ‘Distance to Target’ is set to zero
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’
• the ‘Train Speed’ is set to zero
• the ‘Head End Position’ is set to zero.
I. If the system does not have a track location when enforcement ends in the Current Information:
• the ‘Milepost’, ‘Milepost Prefix Length’, ‘Milepost Suffix Length’, ‘Track Name Length’, ‘PTC Subdivision
/ District ID’, and ‘Current Position Uncertainty’ are set to zero
• the ‘Railroad SCAC’ is populated with ASCII spaces (0x20)
• the ‘Direction of Travel’ is set to ‘0 – Unknown’.
J. The ‘Target Code’ enumeration determines how the ‘Target Description’ field is populated, according to the
following list, where %keyword% indicates variable information available to the onboard segment and will be
replaced with the data in the same format as the corresponding field in the 02083 message expressed in

As a result of the time filter applied, the onboard segment state may be different than when an individual Fault State Change occurred.
design_notes.D: See Section 13 Data Dictionary for mapping between the ‘Locomotive State Summary’ and ‘Locomotive State’ fields.
design_notes.E: The components indicated in this message are populated in the same order as they are listed in the Vendor Component Data Dictionary. The faults are listed according to the order that they change state, with the most recent being listed first. This message is limited to 255 total faults, which are allocated on a firstcome first-served basis. Once the 255 fault limit has been reached, each additional component populates the ‘Number of Fault State Changes’ field with zero. If there are no active faults to report for a component, the ‘Number of Fault State Changes’ field is populated with zero for that component. The faults are independently reported from each source and are not merged.

/// 16 Filesets
16.1 Fileset Definition
EMP messages are utilized to transfer files from the office to the locomotive in groups called filesets. A fileset is
a group of files associated with a repository. Fileset index files describe the contents of a fileset. Each file within
a fileset must have a unique name but different filesets may include the same file.
16.2 Fileset Index File Field Format
The fileset index file is a text file comprised of ASCII characters with line feed (LF) terminated lines; no carriage
returns (CR) are allowed. The fileset index file is named <MD5>.fileset and the MD5 is calculated over the data
in the fileset index file.
Each fileset index file contains a series of fields that are used to identify data in the file. The field format is
shown below using Unix symbol conventions.
<Field Name> <Value> [Value . . .]
Field Name
A field name may be any alphanumeric combination including underscores. Field names are used to identify
following data.
Value
The value is the data that is associated with the field name. Each field name may have one or more values. A
value may contain printable ASCII characters in the range of 0x20 to 0x7E inclusive. When creating a fileset text
file some values must be surrounded by double quotes as specified below. When a value contains a double
quote or a backslash (\) it must be preceded by a backslash (\).
Below is a generic fileset index file. The order of the fields must be observed for interoperable filesets. The order
of the fields does not matter for non-interoperable filesets.
name "<Name>"
vers "<Version>"
rrid "<Railroad SCAC>"
repo "<Repository>"
dest "<Destination>"
file "<file name>" size=<file size in bytes> md5=<file MD5>
file "<file name>" size=<file size in bytes> md5=<file MD5>
.
.
.
name <Name>
The name field is required and occurs once in a fileset index file. This field is a human readable name for the
fileset. The name value is surrounded by double quotes.
vers <Version>
The version (vers) field is required and occurs once in a fileset index file. The version value is surrounded by
double quotes.
rrid <Railroad SCAC>
The railroad ID (rrid) field is required for the railroad specific repositories config and track. It is not used for the
software or common repositories. It occurs once in a fileset index file. This field is populated with the SCAC of
the railroad it represents. The railroad SCAC value is surrounded by double quotes.
repo <Repository>
The repository (repo) field is required and occurs once in a fileset index file. This field contains the repository
associated with the fileset. Valid repositories are listed in Paragraph 13.0, Data Dictionary. The repository value
is surrounded by double quotes.
dest <Destination>
The destination (dest) field is required only when the repository (repo) is set to software and occurs once in a
fileset index file. The destination specifies the platform on which the software is intended to run. The destination
value is surrounded by double quotes.
file <file name> size=<file size in bytes> md5=<file MD5>
The file field is used to describe a file in the fileset. The fileset index file must contain one or more file fields. The
file name must be unique in the fileset. The file name may only be the name of the file and should not include
any directories. The file name value is surrounded by double quotes.
The size field is populated with a decimal integer representing the file size in bytes. The MD5 field is populated
with the 32 lowercase hexadecimal character MD5 calculated over the file. For track and security files, the MD5
is calculated over the unencrypted version of the file.
16.3 Interoperable Fileset Index Files
For software and common configuration filesets from different interoperable railroads to be recognized as being
the same, their version number and MD5 must match.
The governing body assigned by the railroads (ITC) is responsible for maintaining the common configuration.
This includes designating the name and version of each new common configuration fileset.
16.4 Populating Fileset List Messages
The Fileset List (01100) and Client Fileset List (02100) messages are populated with filesets to be downloaded
from the railroad Back Office. The Fileset List (01100) message includes all filesets configured in the railroad
Back Office for the Client groups. The Client Fileset List (02100) message contains all filesets downloaded by
the Client.
Section 16.2 Fileset Index File Field Format specifies which fields should have values surrounded by double
quotes in order to support interoperability. Fileset index files built prior to the addition of these “double quote”
clarifications remain valid and should be included in Fileset List (01100) messages, regardless of the interface
version reported in the Client Fileset List (02100) message.
16.5 Security Repository Structure
This section describes the requirements and structure for the 'Security File' Repository.
16.5.1 Security Fileset Index File Structure
The format of the security fileset index file shall follow the fileset index file format described in Section 16.2
Fileset Index File Field Format.
A security fileset consists of one or more JSON files.
The security fileset is maintained by the owning railroad and uses the "rrid" tag to specify the owner.
The “name” and “vers” are required and are recommended to be meaningful to the supplier of the fileset.
File names in the security fileset index file that do not end in ".json" are ignored.
16.5.2 Security File Structure
All security files are scanned and combined. Any non-matching entries are discarded in the load
process.
Below is the JSON schema for a security file.
security_file.json
{
"description": "security file",
"type": "object",
"properties": {
 "scac": {
 "type": "string",
 "default": "*",
 "description": " Railroad SCAC to match or '*' for any"
 },
 "number": {
 "type": "string",
 "default": "0-999999",
 "description": "a list of comma-separated Locomotive ID number ranges"
 },
 "priority": {
 "type": "integer",
 "default": "0",
 "description": "the priority for the entry, higher = better"
 },
 "system": {
 "type": "string",
 "default": "PTC",
 "description": "the 'System Code' from the Data Dictionary in S-9361"
 },
 "vendor": {
 "type": "string",
 "description": "the 'Vendor Code' from the Data Dictionary in S-9361"
 },
 "users": {
 "type": "object",
 "description": "user info",
 "properties": {
 "username": {
 "type": "string",
 "description": "username"
 },
 "passwd": {
 "type": "string",
 "description": "hashed password"
 },
 "sshpub": {
 "type": "array",
 "contains": {
 "type": "string",
 },
 "description": "one or more public SSH keys in OpenSSH 'ssh-ed25519' format"
 }
 }
 }
},
"required": [
 "users"
]
}
<scac>
The "scac" field is only used if present. If supplied, the value must match the road name from the
locomotive identifier. Case insensitive. The default is "*", which matches any SCAC. If the “scac” field
is present and the value does not match the road name from the locomotive identifier the entry is
discarded.
<number>
The "number" field is only used if present. If supplied, the “number” field must either contain a single
number, multiple numbers separated by commas, a single range or multiple ranges separated by
commas. A range consists of two numbers separated by a ‘-’. The first number must be lower or
equal to the second number.
If the “number” field contains a single number the “number” must match the locomotive number from
the locomotive identifier. If the “number” field contains multiple numbers, one of these numbers must
match the locomotive number from the locomotive identifier. If the “number” field contains one or
more ranges these ranges must include the locomotive number from the locomotive identifier.
If the “number” field contains an empty string, then this entry is discarded. If the “number” field does
not match the locomotive number from the locomotive identifier, then the entry is discarded.
If this field is not present, the default value for the “number” field is “0-999999” which matches any
locomotive number.
Examples:
 "1000" - single number
 "1000-2000" - single range
 "1000,1010,1030" - multiple numbers
 "1000-2000,1010-1030,2000" - multiple ranges
<system>
The "system" field is only used if present. If supplied, it must be "PTC" otherwise, the entry is
discarded.
<vendor>
The "vendor" field is only used if present. If supplied, it must be a value from the ‘Vendor Code’ field
of the Data Dictionary in S-9361 otherwise the entry is discarded
<priority>
The "priority" field is only used if present. Entries with a negative priority are discarded. <username>
Valid usernames, e.g., "maint" and "support".
<passwd>
The "passwd" value is stored in the systems secure password repository. If multiple entries for the
same user are included in the fileset, only the “passwd” from the entry with the highest priority is
stored.
The following glibc-compatible encryption algorithms are supported:
1 = MD5
5 = SHA-256
6 = SHA-512
Use of 5 (SHA-256) is recommended
<sshpub>
The "sshpub" value(s) are stored in the secure authorized keys repository for the user. If multiple
entries for the same user are included in the fileset, the “sshpub” values from each entry are added
to the user’s authorized keys repository. Refer to the OpenSSH documentation for the
"authorized_keys" format.
